summary: Round 1's fixes hold. The placement output is checked before anything is posted, a 422 is recognised when its body has no status, the clone's diff ignores GIT_DIFF_OPTS, and a comment with no path moves into the body again; each fix has a case. The findings left are inputs the new paths assume away: a NUL in a recovered hunk, git attributes that make a text file binary in the clone, a fixture made under the developer's git config, and one temp file made before the scratch folder exists. Nothing in this repository is scheduled or queued against these files, so no overlap applies.

findings.title: One NUL byte in the recovered hunks makes grep drop every file marker, so every patch-less file's comments go to the body
findings.description: The hunks file holds raw diff lines, and three plain `grep $'^@@@redline-file\t'` calls read the file markers out of it: here in recover_hunks (`found`), at 428 in place_comments (`recovered`) and at 720 in post-review (`sourced`). grep treats a file holding a NUL as binary. I checked both halves on this machine. Homebrew gawk keeps a NUL through `{print}` (od shows `-   a  \0   b`), so diff_sections writes it into the hunks file. macOS /usr/bin/awk (20200816) truncates the line at the NUL instead, so the default macOS awk is not exposed. On a file holding `@@@redline-file\tsrc/big.js` and a hunk line with a NUL, the system grep prints `Binary file /tmp/redlinerepro/nul-hunks.txt matches` instead of the marker line, and `cut -f2` passes that line through as a path. GNU grep 3.5 and later prints nothing on stdout and `grep: <file>: binary file matches` on stderr. Either way no real path reaches `found` or `recovered`. In place_comments (lines 433-438) every wanted file therefore gets kind `nopatch` and is not `hunks`, so every comment on every patch-less file in the review, not only the one with the NUL, moves under "The file's patch could not be had from GitHub's listing, its whole diff or this clone". That line is false, because the hunks were found. recover_hunks also sees every file as missing and appends the clone's sections again. `sourced` is empty too, so a later refusal is never acted on. Conditions: a text file over about 100 KiB with a NUL after its first 8,000 bytes, which git's binary check does not look at, so git and the whole diff treat it as text with hunks; a GNU awk or mawk first on PATH (any Linux runner, or gawk installed as awk); and one comment on any patch-less file of that review. What GitHub's listing gives for such a file could not be checked from here.
findings.proposedFix: Read the markers so a NUL cannot hide them: `grep -a $'^@@@redline-file\t'` at the three sites, or `awk -F'\t' '/^@@@redline-file\t/ {print $2}'`. Add a gh-test case with a NUL past byte 8,000 in a recovered section, run under gawk.

findings.title: The clone's pinned git diff still follows git attributes and core.bigFileThreshold, so a text file can come back binary with no hunks
findings.description: The command at 371-373 pins the algorithm, the context, the prefixes, renames, `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, but not git's decision that a file is binary. That decision comes from attributes, which git reads from the repository's `.gitattributes`, from `.git/info/attributes`, and from `core.attributesFile` (which defaults to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes`, or `~/.config/git/attributes`; git-config(1), lines 3709-3719 of the local man page). It also comes from `core.bigFileThreshold`: files above it "will be treated as if they were labeled binary ... git-diff will not compute diffs" (git-config(1), lines 3662-3667). For a path whose `diff` attribute is unset, git writes `Binary files ... differ` (gitattributes(5), line 843), so its section has no `@@ ` line. diff_sections (line 317) prints a section only from its first `@@ ` line on, so the file gets no hunks and its comments move under the could-not-be-had line, although GitHub would take them inline. A user-level `package-lock.json -diff` or `*.lock binary` is the common case, and lockfiles are among the files over 100 KiB this feature is for. The recover_hunks comment (lines 333-335) and the bash-conventions line this fix diff rewrote both promise that "the user's git configuration and environment cannot move a hunk". The case at gh-test.sh line 483 pins only `diff.*` keys. Conditions: the clone is the source (a pull request over 300 files, or a refused or missing section in the whole diff), and the local attributes or threshold mark a file binary that GitHub treats as text. The guard refuses `git -c` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=` to this role, so I traced this through git's documentation and the code rather than running it. The coverage pass reports a run of it on PR 21: 0 hunks without `--text` and 2 with it.
findings.proposedFix: Add `--text` to the pinned `git diff`: a wanted file is text by GitHub's listing (`changes` above 0). Add a gh-test case beside the pinned-configuration one, with a global `core.attributesFile` marking `lib/local.txt -diff`, and add `--text` to the pinned flag list in agent-os/standards/scripts/bash-conventions.md.

findings.title: pr_files makes its temp file before the scratch folder exists, so an interrupt can still leave one behind
findings.description: R1-2's fix makes the scratch folder after `all="$(pr_files "$1")"` (place, line 535; post-review, line 706). pr_files makes `redline-gh.XXXXXX` in the real TMPDIR (line 261) and removes it only on its own return paths (lines 265, 269, 272). An interrupt during its paginated `gh api` call, which is the longest read on a large pull request, leaves that file behind. The comment the fix added (lines 536-538 and 707-709) says every temp file of the subcommand is made in the folder the trap removes. The standard it added to bash-conventions.md says a subcommand's temp files, "directly or through the functions it calls", are all made there, "so a failure or an interrupt leaves nothing". The leftover-file cases at gh-test.sh lines 360-365 pass because they fail after pr_files. pr_files' temp file predates this pull request; the claim that covers it is in R1-2's fix.
findings.proposedFix: Make the scratch folder, set its trap and point TMPDIR at it before `all="$(pr_files "$1")"` in both place and post-review.

findings.title: The fixture's whole diff follows the developer's git config and GIT_DIFF_OPTS, so the patch-less cases can fail locally
findings.description: diff-20.txt, which the shim serves as GitHub's whole diff for PR 20, is made at line 173 with `git -C "$GEN" -c core.quotepath=true diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ -M`. That command does not pin `-U3`, `--diff-algorithm`, `--inter-hunk-context` or `--indent-heuristic`, and it does not unset GIT_DIFF_OPTS. The harness sets neither GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL nor GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM (lines 69-76). So a developer with `diff.context = 0` in their config, or with GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0 exported, gets a fixture with no context lines. src/big.js changes at line 100 (line 138), so RIGHT 98 is a context line only under -U3. review-20-text's R1-3 (line 187) then leaves the hunks, and the context-line cases fail. `diff.interHunkContext` merges hunks the same way. The script's own clone diff is pinned (R1-4), so only the fixture is exposed. gen_commit (line 126) also runs under the developer's global config and hooks. CI runs with the default config and is not affected. The guard does not let this role run the harness, so this is traced, not run. The coverage pass reports 3 failures under each setting.
findings.proposedFix: Make diff-20.txt with the script's pinned flags under `env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS`, or run every git call of the harness with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and GIT_DIFF_OPTS unset.

list.summary: On Linux, one NUL byte in a recovered hunk moves every comment on a patch-less file into the review body. They land under "The file's patch could not be had from GitHub's listing, its whole diff or this clone", which is false because the hunks were found, and grep prints "binary file matches" on stderr. Three plain `grep $'^@@@redline-file\t'` calls read the hunks file, which holds raw diff lines: here in recover_hunks (`found`), at 428 in place_comments (`recovered`) and at 720 in post-review (`sourced`). GNU and BSD grep treat a file with a NUL as binary, so GNU grep prints no marker and BSD grep prints "Binary file ... matches", which cut passes on as a path. macOS awk drops the NUL first, so only GNU or mawk awk is exposed. Fix: read the markers with `grep -a` (or `LC_ALL=C grep -a`), or pull them out with `awk -F'\t' '/^@@@redline-file\t/ {print $2}'`, and add a gh-test case with a NUL past byte 8000 in a recovered file.
list.failure_scenario: Reproduced with GNU awk 5.4 and GNU grep 3.12 on PATH. In diff-20.txt I put a NUL into one removed line of lib/gone.txt, then ran `place 20` with comments on src/big.js:1500 and lib/gone.txt:10 LEFT. Both moved under the could-not-be-had line, and stderr showed `grep: .../redline-gh.XXXX: binary file matches` twice. Without the NUL both are placed inline. A text file over 100 KiB with a NUL after its first 8000 bytes is text to git and to GitHub (changes > 0, no patch), so its hunks carry the NUL. The trigger is a Linux runner (Ubuntu CI, GNU tools) and one comment on such a file.

list.summary: The clone's diff still follows git attributes, so a large text file marked `-diff` or `binary` gets no hunks from the clone. The same happens to a file over a lowered `core.bigFileThreshold`. Its comments go into the body as "could not be had" although GitHub would take them. The pinned flags block textconv and external diffs but not git's binary decision, which comes from the repo's .gitattributes, the user's `core.attributesFile` (default ~/.config/git/attributes) or `core.bigFileThreshold`. Lockfiles marked `package-lock.json -diff` are exactly the files over 100 KiB that this feature is for, on PRs over 300 files or when the whole diff is refused. This breaks the promise in the recover_hunks comment and in scripts/bash-conventions that "the user's git configuration and environment cannot move a hunk". Fix: add `--text` to the pinned `git diff` (a wanted file is text in GitHub's listing, changes > 0), add a case beside the pinned-configuration one, and add `--text` to the pinned flag list in bash-conventions.
list.failure_scenario: Reproduced on the harness's PR 21 (301 files, so the clone is the only source). With GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL setting `core.attributesFile` to a file holding `lib/local.txt -diff`, `place 21` moved R1-1, R1-2 and R1-3 under the could-not-be-had line, where the default run places R1-1 and R1-2 inline. `core.bigFileThreshold = 100k` gave the same result. The script's exact git diff command gave 0 hunks without `--text` and 2 hunks with it, in both cases.

list.summary: tests/gh-test.sh fails for a contributor whose own git diff settings differ from the defaults. The fixture's whole diff (diff-20.txt) is made with the developer's git config and environment, so GitHub's hunks are not what the place cases test against. The command pins prefixes, color, external diff, renames and quoting, but not `-U3`, `--diff-algorithm`, `--inter-hunk-context` or `--indent-heuristic`, and it does not unset GIT_DIFF_OPTS. gen_commit also runs the developer's global commit hooks. Fix: make diff-20.txt with the script's pinned flags under `env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS`, or run the harness's own git with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.
list.failure_scenario: Reproduced. Run with `diff.context = 0` in the global config, or with GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0 exported, the suite reports 251 passed and 3 failed. The failures are the patch-less text file cases ("an added, a removed and a context line stay inline", "nothing is moved", "the body is left alone"), because the context line RIGHT 98 leaves the fixture's hunk. With `diff.interHunkContext = 1000` the three `place: causes` cases fail, because src/big.js:500 lands inside a merged hunk.
